issues.where: README.md: Components; tokens.json: drawer, hover-card, tabs, leaderboard and select usage references
issues.problem: The system references essential watch surfaces and controls but provides buildable specifications only for StatusBox, MatrixCell and Counter.
issues.why: Agents must invent the matrix structure, leaderboard, navigation, detail panel and supporting controls independently.
issues.fix: Add normative component specs and reference markup for Matrix, Leaderboard, Tabs, DetailPanel, Tooltip, Button, Select and ThemeToggle. Define matrix and leaderboard row/column headers using native tables; use 36px-minimum desktop rows, 16px column gaps and existing surface tokens. Define a modal detail panel at min(480px, 100vw), with bg, 24px padding, 28px section gaps, a labelled heading, focus containment, Escape dismissal and focus restoration. Specify tab arrow-key behavior, sort-button aria-sort updates, disabled-control behavior, and tooltip opening on focus as well as hover, Escape dismissal and touch access.

issues.where: README.md: Components; components/Counter/README.md: Provide and Finished
issues.problem: There are no application-level specifications for initial loading, an empty run, no matching results or a disconnected watch stream.
issues.why: An agent must invent these layouts and may present missing or stale data as a valid zero or completed run.
issues.fix: Add an application-state table: loading shows 'Loading run…' with no numeric result; zero cells shows 'No cells in this run.' with no percentage; an empty filter shows 'No evals match these filters.' and a 'Clear filters' button; disconnection retains the last data and shows 'Connection lost. Showing the last update from {time}.' with 'Reconnect'. Use body text in fg on surface, 24px padding and 12px content gaps; connection warnings use yellow on yellow-tint. Never convert loading, missing data or disconnection into PASS, 0% or Finished.

issues.where: components/StatusBox/README.md: phone rule; components/MatrixCell/README.md: phone rules; components/Counter/README.md: phone rules; components/bundle.css
issues.problem: Phone adaptations exist only as scattered prose, lack responsive CSS, and explicitly drop the brackets despite the required bracket-framed sample treatment.
issues.why: Agents will choose different breakpoints and overflow behavior, and some will remove the product's defining matrix frame.
issues.fix: Define phone as viewport width below 640px and compile responsive rules: app padding 16px; counter 36px, finished counter 24px; cell min-height 32px; boxes 10px with radius-2; elapsed retained and ETA hidden. Retain brackets at every width. Put wide matrices in their own horizontally scrollable region with a sticky eval-label column and the specified 8px shade gradient; allow the surrounding page to reflow at 320px. Specify compact labels as '{finished}/{total} · {state}' and retain accessible full labels and non-color status cues.

issues.where: components/MatrixCell/README.md: Label; components/Counter/README.md: Provide; components/MatrixCell/preview.html: error example
issues.problem: Pooled rates, cell completion and tally categories lack a deterministic aggregation contract, especially for mixed errors, timeouts and n/a samples.
issues.why: Agents can calculate different benchmark results and completion totals from the same run.
issues.fix: Add a backend-to-UI data contract containing rate numerator, rate denominator, applicable-check scope, sample state, cell terminal flag and run terminal reason. Require the UI to use the backend's canonical eligibility policy rather than infer a rate from box colors or sample counts. Specify rate = 100 × numerator / denominator, denominator zero displays '—', in-flight rates remain provisional, and all-error cells retain the error marker. Specify N as terminal included cells, M as run.start.cell_count, and tally buckets as mutually exclusive with an explicit mapping for timeout, quiet, booting and n/a. Add fixtures for mixed outcomes and interrupted runs.

issues.problem: The hover selector has greater specificity than the selected selector, so hovering a selected cell replaces its 2px selection ring with the 1px hover ring.
issues.why: The visible selected state changes merely because the pointer enters it, contradicting the documented state model.
issues.fix: Exclude selected cells from the ordinary hover rule, then add '.bs-cell.bs-sel, .bs-cell.bs-sel:hover { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--accent); }' and '.bs-cell.bs-sel:hover { background: var(--hover); }'. Document that selection persists through hover and keyboard focus, with the external focus outline remaining independently visible.

issues.problem: The progress component has no accessible progress semantics or rule for announcing live updates.
issues.why: An agent may expose an unnamed decorative bar or announce every elapsed-time tick instead of useful run changes.
issues.fix: Give the bar role='progressbar', aria-label='Run completion', aria-valuemin='0', aria-valuemax=M, aria-valuenow=N and aria-valuetext='{N} of {M} cells finished'. For unknown totals, omit aria-valuenow; for M=0, use the empty-run state instead. Add a separate polite, atomic status region announcing completion-count changes at most once every 10 seconds and the terminal run state immediately; do not place elapsed time or streaming logs in that region.

issues.where: components/bundle.css: hardcoded spacing and type values; tokens.json: spacing and type
issues.problem: Component rules copy tokenized values as literals and introduce unregistered values such as 3px padding and the 20px Finished label.
issues.why: Changing the token source will leave component geometry and typography behind, creating two competing systems.
issues.fix: Replace component spacing literals with the existing space-* variables and expose type styles as generated custom-property groups consumed by components. Add space-3 = 3px and a finished-label style using DM Sans, 20px, line-height 1 and weight 500. Make tokens.json the only source for these values and add a build check rejecting unregistered spacing, radius and typography literals in production component CSS.

issues.where: components/bundle.css: Google Fonts @import; tokens.json: type.fonts; README.md: Type
issues.problem: The supplied stylesheet fetches fonts externally even though watch's documented content security policy blocks them and the font manifest is empty.
issues.why: An agent copying the bundle will render system fallbacks instead of the specified UI typography, particularly offline.
issues.fix: Remove the Google Fonts import. Populate type.fonts with local WOFF2 paths and license metadata for DM Mono 400/500 and DM Sans 400/500 with the specified optical-size range. Generate same-origin @font-face declarations with font-display: swap, ship those files with watch, and verify the component previews under default-src 'self' with network access disabled.

issues.where: README.md: Logo / Wordmark and Type; assets/Logos/benchspec-wordmark-light.svg; assets/Logos/benchspec-wordmark-dark.svg
issues.problem: The wordmark uses platform-dependent live text while raster assets use different platform fonts and weights.
issues.why: Maintainers and agents cannot reproduce a single wordmark shape across operating systems, README assets and watch.
issues.fix: Adopt DM Mono Medium 500 as the named wordmark face, replace the prohibition against DM Mono, and update wordmark and social-wordmark tokens to weight 500. Generate outlined text paths for both distributed wordmark SVGs from the same pinned font file, retaining the accessible benchspec name. Use that same font source for raster artwork and document the approved outlined assets as authoritative.

issues.problem: There is no standalone dark-ground mark asset, so a routine dark-background placement requires manual recoloring.
issues.why: An agent or maintainer may reuse the light-ground file on navy or generate a slightly different dark variant.
issues.fix: Ship benchspec-mark-dark.svg with the existing geometry, brackets #E8ECF1, left squares #6E7891, right squares 1 and 3 #F0764B, and middle-right square #F2A48C. Identify the existing file explicitly as the light-ground variant and document file selection for external images versus wm-* bindings for inline UI SVG.

Q1.answer: Yes. Adopt DM Mono Medium 500, a free Google Fonts family, as the named wordmark face and distribute outlined SVG wordmarks.
Q1.why: A pinned face removes platform-dependent letterforms and synthetic weight differences without introducing another font family. Its restrained monospace character connects the identity to benchmark data; the bracket-matrix mark remains the primary distinctive element.

Q2.answer: Keep DM Mono and DM Sans; do not replace the UI pairing. Self-host both and make their role assignments executable through generated styles.
Q2.why: Replacing the families would not address the demonstrated failures: blocked font loading, contradictory usage guidance and incomplete component behavior. Retain DM Mono for identifiers, code and aligned data, and DM Sans for prose and navigation, with tabular numerals wherever values align.

top_three: Make the supplied components accessible by default: non-color sample distinctions, semantic keyboard-operable cells, implemented focus styles and a running indicator that retains contrast throughout its animation.
Publish a complete watch contract covering missing surfaces, aggregation semantics, loading and connection states, and responsive behavior while retaining the bracketed sample motif.
Make production output deterministic: choose status encoding over the experimental ramp, generate component values from tokens, self-host UI fonts and ship reproducible light/dark logo assets.

issues.where: components/StatusBox/README.md: state table; components/bundle.css: .bs-b-pass, .bs-b-fail, .bs-b-to; components/MatrixCell/README.md: Markers
issues.problem: Pass, fail and timeout use the same filled-square shape, while phone rules remove text markers that distinguish additional states.
issues.why: An agent following these rules would produce sample results that depend on color, despite the explicit claim that shape carries state.
issues.fix: Keep pass as a solid neutral square; add a 2px knockout X inside fail and a 2px knockout horizontal bar inside timeout, using the actual surrounding ground color for the knockout. Give quiet a square center rather than running's round dot. Retain exception text on phones, allowing it to wrap below the boxes. Give every sample an accessible description such as 'Sample 2: FAIL' and update the legend with the same shapes.

issues.problem: The executable examples implement interactive cells as unfocusable divs and omit the documented focus treatment.
issues.why: An agent copying the examples would make sample details inaccessible from the keyboard.
issues.fix: Render actionable cells as button elements with type='button', aria-haspopup='dialog', aria-controls pointing to the drawer, and aria-expanded reflecting its state. Include eval, arm and summary in the accessible name. Render 'not run' as noninteractive text. Add '.bs-cell:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }', reset native button borders and alignment, and ensure containers do not clip the outline. Enter and Space open details; closing restores focus to the triggering cell.

issues.where: components/bundle.css: .bs-b-run and @keyframes bs-pulse; contrast.md: meaningful-mark coverage
issues.problem: The running animation reduces the entire status mark to 45% opacity, invalidating the opaque-color contrast guarantee.
issues.why: An agent would ship a running ring that falls below 3:1 during its pulse even though the contrast table reports a pass.
issues.fix: Keep the running ring and dot at opacity 1 throughout. Move the dot into a 5px circular pseudo-element and animate only its scale from 1 to 0.7 and back over 1.6s; keep the 2px ring static. Under prefers-reduced-motion, disable the transform animation. Extend contrast checks to rendered component states rather than opaque token pairs alone.

issues.where: README.md: Color / Pass-rate ramp; tokens.json: rate-0 through rate-100
issues.problem: The production token set exposes an unchosen rate-color alternative that conflicts with the specified status encoding.
issues.why: An agent must decide whether sample boxes represent categorical outcomes or pass-rate bands, producing incompatible interfaces.
issues.fix: Add the normative rule: 'watch sample boxes always use StatusBox categorical states; rate-* tokens must not be used in production watch.' Move the ramp to an experimental token file excluded from the default build, and remove instructions to fill sample boxes with it from the production documentation.

issues.problem: Component typography and spacing are copied literals rather than references to the declared source of truth, and some type properties are omitted.
issues.why: An agent updating tokens would leave components unchanged or inherit unintended values, such as the cell's 1.55 line height instead of 1.2.
issues.fix: Generate size, line-height, weight and tracking custom properties for every type role from tokens.json. For cells emit --type-cell-size: 13.5px, --type-cell-leading: 1.2 and --type-cell-weight: 400, then consume all three in .bs-cell. Replace existing component spacing literals with their space-* references. Add explicit tokens for currently prose-only variants, including counter-phone: 36px, counter-finished-phone: 24px and finished-label: 20px/1 at weight 500. Generate published and review CSS through the same compiler.

issues.where: components/StatusBox/README.md: phone sizing; components/MatrixCell/README.md: phone rules; components/Counter/README.md: phone rules
issues.problem: Phone behavior is scattered through prose without a shared breakpoint or implementation, and dropping brackets contradicts the required sample framing.
issues.why: An agent must invent responsive layout rules and may remove the brand's bracket-matrix motif on phones.
issues.fix: Define phone as viewport width below 640px and implement it in the shared stylesheet: 16px app padding, 10px sample boxes with 2px radii, cells with min-height 32px and auto height for wrapping, counter sizes 36px live and 24px finished, and no ETA. Preserve brackets at both sizes. Put only the matrix in a horizontally scrollable region, use a 120px sticky eval-label column and arm columns with min-width 160px, and keep the rest of the page reflowing at 320px. Specify compact labels as 'N/M · running', 'booting', 'queued', 'n/a' or 'not run', with exception text retained.

issues.where: README.md: Components; tokens.json: bg, raised, shade and type.tab usage
issues.problem: The system references drawers, hover cards, tabs, sortable leaderboards and controls without supplying their component contracts.
issues.why: An agent must invent the main watch navigation and detail surfaces despite having tokens that imply they are already designed.
issues.fix: Add normative specs and executable examples for MatrixTable, Leaderboard, Tabs, SampleDrawer, HoverCard and shared controls. Define table header associations, group disclosure and sorting behavior. Specify the drawer as a modal dialog on bg, 480px wide on desktop and a full-width bottom sheet below 640px, with 24px padding, radius-8, Escape-to-close, contained focus and focus restoration. Specify hover cards as bg with 12px padding and shadow-hovercard. Use native buttons/selects, 36px desktop and 44px phone control heights, the shared focus outline, and disabled states with disabled semantics and no hover response.

issues.where: components/Counter/README.md: Provide and Finished; README.md: Components
issues.problem: Initial loading, empty runs, disconnected streams and interrupted runs have no specified presentation.
issues.why: An agent must improvise lifecycle states and could show stale data as live or label an interrupted run 'Finished'.
issues.fix: Add a lifecycle state table: loading shows 'Loading run…' with aria-busy='true' and no fabricated percentage; zero cells shows 'No samples in this run.' and no progress bar; connection loss preserves results and shows 'Connection lost. Reconnecting…' with the live indicator removed; interruption shows 'Run stopped · N of M finished' and preserves actual progress. Show 'Finished' only after a completed-run event. Use body/help typography, fg/muted text and existing surfaces for these states, with a polite status region announcing transitions.

issues.where: components/MatrixCell/README.md: Label and Markers; components/Counter/README.md: counts and tally
issues.problem: The docs do not define aggregation, mixed-state precedence or how timeout and n/a affect completion and tally counts.
issues.why: An agent could calculate different rates and completion totals from the same run or hide one exception behind another.
issues.fix: Add a data contract naming backend-authoritative pooled rate, finished-cell count, total-cell count and state counts; explicitly prohibit deriving pooled rate from the number of pass-colored boxes. Define all terminal sample states, including timeout, error and n/a, for completion purposes, and exclude 'not run' cells from run totals. Set progress width to 100 × finished/total, round displayed progress to the nearest integer and handle total=0 separately. For mixed cells show completed/total plus active phase, list every present exception with counts in error, timeout, quiet order, and use the longest silence duration for quiet.

issues.where: components/StatusBox/preview.html: .bs-lg title attributes; components/MatrixCell/README.md: per-sample detail
issues.problem: Legend explanations rely on native title tooltips, and hover detail has no keyboard or touch behavior.
issues.why: An agent would leave definitions unavailable to touch users and inconsistently exposed to keyboard users.
issues.fix: Replace title-only definitions with a 'Status definitions' disclosure containing the nine visible name-and-definition pairs. If custom tooltips remain, specify appearance on hover and focus, aria-describedby linkage, Escape dismissal, pointer access to the tooltip and persistence until hover/focus leaves. State that every hover-card detail is also available through the keyboard- and touch-operable cell drawer.

issues.problem: The hover selector has greater specificity than the selected selector and replaces the selected cell's 2px ring with a 1px ring.
issues.why: An agent using the supplied CSS would make selection appear weaker or disappear when the pointer enters the selected cell.
issues.fix: Add '.bs-cell.bs-sel, .bs-cell.bs-sel:hover { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--accent); }' after the hover rules. Document state composition: hover changes the ground, selection retains its 2px inset ring, and keyboard focus adds the separate 2px offset outline.

issues.where: components/bundle.css: Google Fonts @import; tokens.json: type.fonts; README.md: Type
issues.problem: The only supplied font-loading implementation uses Google Fonts despite watch's self-only content security policy, and the font manifest is empty.
issues.why: An agent copying the stylesheet would silently render fallback fonts in the actual product rather than the documented UI pairing.
issues.fix: Remove the remote @import and populate type.fonts with local assets and licenses. Ship DM Mono 400/500 and DM Sans 400/500 as WOFF2 under /assets/fonts/, with self-hosted @font-face declarations and font-display: swap. Specify font-style: normal and the exact supported weights; retain system stacks only as loading or failure fallbacks. Add an offline, CSP-enabled rendering test.

issues.problem: The wordmark is live system-font text while raster assets use separate platform-dependent fonts, so the identity changes across machines.
issues.why: Agents and maintainers cannot reproduce one consistent wordmark across README, social artwork and watch.
issues.fix: Adopt DM Mono Medium 500 as the named wordmark face, replace the prohibition on DM Mono, and outline the wordmark text in both distributed SVGs. Keep an editable source using 30px DM Mono 500 at x=72, baseline y=43 in the existing 250×64 viewBox. Pin the same font files in the asset renderer, use DM Mono 500 for the social wordmark and 400 for its tagline, and update the weight rules to match.

issues.problem: There is no standalone dark-ground mark asset, so consumers must modify the light-ground SVG themselves.
issues.why: Maintainers using image embeds or external asset tools cannot apply CSS tokens and may ship invisible navy brackets or inconsistent recoloring.
issues.fix: Generate benchspec-mark-dark.svg using brackets #E8ECF1, left squares #6E7891, right squares 1 and 3 #F0764B, and middle-right square #F2A48C. Preserve the existing geometry and accessible label. Document the existing mark as the light-ground variant and provide a picture-element example selecting between the two files.

Q1.answer: Yes. Adopt DM Mono Medium 500, a free Google Fonts family, as the named wordmark face and distribute outlined SVG wordmarks.
Q1.why: The problem is reproducibility, not a need for a more decorative font. Reusing DM Mono removes platform-dependent letterforms, connects the identity to watch's data typography and avoids adding a third family.

Q2.answer: Yes—retain DM Mono and DM Sans. Specify DM Mono for identifiers, code, numeric results and compact data labels; DM Sans for navigation, prose, explanations and action labels.
Q2.why: A replacement would not resolve the observed implementation gaps. The priority is reliable self-hosting, complete type-role bindings and tabular numerals wherever values align, rather than introducing another visual direction.

top_three: Make the supplied components accessible in practice: non-color sample encodings, semantic keyboard-operable cells, visible focus and a contrast-safe running animation.
Complete the watch contract with responsive layouts, detail surfaces, lifecycle states and authoritative aggregation rules so agents do not invent product behavior.
Create one deterministic production source: exclude the experimental ramp, generate component styles from tokens, self-host UI fonts and freeze the wordmark artwork.

issues.problem: Pass, fail and timeout are the same filled square and differ only by hue, and fail has no text marker, so a mixed cell conveys which sample failed by color alone.
issues.why: An agent shipping the StatusBox CSS will leave a color-blind user unable to tell a failed sample from a passed one when the cell label is only a pooled rate such as 67%.
issues.fix: Keep pass a solid status-pass square. Draw fail as a status-fail fill plus a 1.5px bg X (two diagonals covering 42–58% of the 14px box). Draw timeout as a status-timeout fill plus a 2px bg bar at 50% height, and keep the timeout marker. Give every box role="img" and an aria-label (pass, fail, timeout, error, running, booting, quiet, queued, n/a). Do not recolor pass to green.

issues.problem: Matrix cells are clickable but bundle.css has no :focus-visible rule, the box is an empty <i>, and MatrixCell puts per-sample detail on hover only.
issues.why: An agent copying the stylesheet will build a pointer-only matrix, so keyboard and screen-reader users cannot open a cell or hear which sample failed.
issues.fix: Make .bs-cell a <button type="button">. Add .bs-cell:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; } and keep selection as box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--accent) so the two stack. Open the hover card on focus as well as hover. Enter moves focus into the drawer; Esc closes it and returns focus to the cell.

issues.problem: The value style says the best leaderboard cell takes accent, but light accent #DF4A19 is only 3.25–4.09:1 on UI grounds, under the 4.5:1 text floor.
issues.why: An agent following the type token will color the best rate with accent, which matches accent-ink in dark and fails WCAG on every light ground.
issues.fix: Change the value usage to: the best per row is accent-ink (#A93F18 light, #F0764B dark), never accent. Add .bs-value-best { color: var(--accent-ink); } and the word best beside the mark so the diamond is not the only signal.

issues.problem: The running pulse fades the whole box to opacity 0.45, so the 2px accent ring, the only non-text running signal, drops below 3:1 on raised for half of the 1.6s cycle.
issues.why: In a mixed cell the label does not name the running sample, so that box will look empty, like queued, twice a second.
issues.fix: Keep the ring at full opacity. Pulse only the centre dot: .bs-b-run::after { width: 5px; height: 5px; background: var(--status-running); animation: bs-pulse 1.6s ease-in-out infinite; } and under prefers-reduced-motion set animation: none; opacity: 1. Remove the opacity animation from .bs-b-run itself.

issues.problem: Drawer, hover card, leaderboard, tabs, phase bar, assertions, theme toggle, empty, disabled and loading are named by tokens and have no component spec.
issues.why: An agent will invent those surfaces, so the main watch flows will not match the product or the tokens that already assume them.
issues.fix: Add three specs. Drawer: 420px desktop, full-width phone sheet, padding space-24, radius-8, shadow-sheet on phone, eval-id header, sans status line such as FAIL · 6/9 assertions, assertion rows with ✓ in ok and ✗ in red plus the words pass and fail, Esc closes. Hover card: radius-8, padding space-12, shadow-hovercard, 1px line border (the black 0.35 shadow is invisible on #14172E), opens on hover and focus. Leaderboard: odd rows surface, even rows band, sticky lbl column, best cell accent-ink plus the word best. Empty copy: No run yet. Disabled: faint text, no opacity, cursor not-allowed. Loading: booting boxes and the label booting, no spinner.

issues.problem: The 640px phone breakpoint and every phone size live only in usage prose, and there is no column, sticky-matrix or sheet token.
issues.why: An agent parsing tokens.json will ship 44px counters and 36px cells on a phone, or invent a breakpoint and a stacking layout the docs never define.
issues.fix: Add breakpoint-phone: 640px. Set structured sizes: counter 44/36, counter-finished 30/24, heading 30/24, status 16/15, size-cell 36/32, page padding 28px 36px desktop and 16px phone. Under 640px drop brackets, hide markers, drop the ETA, scroll the matrix horizontally, and pin the label column with an 8px shade-to-transparent gradient. Four-arm cells use size-box-phone (10px) and drop brackets on desktop too.

issues.problem: The pass-rate ramp is described as not yet chosen and, in the same paragraph, as the fill for sample boxes, which contradicts StatusBox.
issues.why: An agent will either recolor boxes with rate-0–rate-100 or ignore eleven tokens, and the two builds will not look like one product.
issues.fix: Delete rate-0 through rate-100 from tokens.json and tokens.css. Replace that Color paragraph with: Sample boxes use StatusBox states only. Do not encode pass rate as a fill. Print the pooled rate beside the boxes in fg.

issues.problem: The font source of truth is fonts: [], while bundle.css imports Google Fonts, which the watch CSP default-src 'self' blocks.
issues.why: An agent will hotlink Google Fonts and get a silent fallback, or guess file names, so watch will not actually render in DM Mono and DM Sans.
issues.fix: Self-host the woff2 files and set fonts to DM Mono 400 and 500 plus DM Sans 400 and 500, opsz 9–40, with those paths. Replace the @import with @font-face rules that use local urls only. Keep the current family stacks as the fallback.

issues.problem: Voice requires uppercase PASS, FAIL, TIMEOUT and ERROR, but StatusBox, MatrixCell and the tally use lowercase pass, fail, timeout, error and 4 failed.
issues.why: An agent will uppercase cell labels and the legend, breaking the MatrixCell plain-words rule and disagreeing with the terminal.
issues.fix: Replace the voice bullet with: Watch UI uses lowercase state words: pass, fail, timeout, error, queued, running, booting, quiet 52s, n/a, not run. Uppercase PASS, FAIL, TIMEOUT and ERROR are only for the terminal report and the drawer status line (FAIL · 6/9 assertions). Tallies use 4 failed and 0 errored.

issues.problem: Bracket frames use opacity 0.7, 3px 6px padding, a 1.5px stroke and a 2.5px dot, none of which are tokens or written in the StatusBox spec.
issues.why: An agent following the README will draw full-strength faint brackets, while an agent copying the CSS will fade them, so the logo echo will not match across builds.
issues.fix: Add --size-bracket-stroke: 1.5px, --space-bracket-y: 3px, --space-bracket-x: 6px and --size-dot: 5px. Document them in StatusBox. Set bracket opacity to 1 so the frame stays at faint's measured 5.35:1 on dark surface, and delete the 0.7.

issues.problem: The type scale is not closed: social-wordmark is weight 700, the Finished word is 20px, cell is 13.5px and marker is 11.5px, against a rule of weights 400 and 500 plus wordmark 600.
issues.why: An agent will load a bold the UI families do not include, or invent a 20px step, and the README lockup will not match the SVG wordmark.
issues.fix: Set social-wordmark fontWeight to 600. Change the Finished word from 20px to the title size, 18px sans 500. Snap cell to 14px and marker to 12px. Set help line-height to 1.4 and delete the 1.5 versus 1.4 split. Add font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums to counter, metric, value, cell and body-mono.

issues.problem: Light band and light raised are both #E9EBF2, status-pass is an alias of the text token faint, and accent-tint is used by no component.
issues.why: An agent will put a raised tile on a banded row and it will vanish in the light theme, or invent a one-off use for accent-tint.
issues.fix: Add this rule: light band equals light raised on purpose; leaderboard rows alternate surface #FFFFFF and band #E9EBF2 and must not contain raised tiles. Keep status-pass at the current hex but stop calling it a text color so the fill can move later. Delete accent-tint.

issues.problem: Chrome icons are required as DM Mono glyphs (✓ ✗ › ‹ › ▸ ▼ ◆), and that face does not contain those codepoints, while the wordmark uses a different mono.
issues.why: An agent will get fallback glyphs that break the monospace grid, or substitute emoji, which the voice rules forbid.
issues.fix: Replace those glyphs with 12px currentColor SVGs named check, x, chevron-left, chevron-right, caret-right, caret-down, diamond and close, and specify the paths in Iconography. Do not set them in DM Mono. Keep the wordmark on the wordmark stack only until it is outlined.

issues.problem: There is no dark-ground mark file, and both wordmarks are live SVG text, so Menlo, Consolas and Liberation Mono draw different widths in the 250×64 viewBox.
issues.why: An agent embedding benchspec-mark.svg on navy will lose the brackets, and the top-bar wordmark will shift or overflow by OS.
issues.fix: Add benchspec-mark-dark.svg with brackets #E8ECF1, left squares #6E7891, right squares #F0764B and #F2A48C. Outline both wordmarks as paths in IBM Plex Mono 600 so the 250×64 box no longer depends on installed fonts. Keep the existing don't list.

Q1.answer: Yes. Adopt IBM Plex Mono (Google Fonts, OFL) at weight 600 and outline it into the wordmark SVGs.
Q1.why: The wordmark has no font of its own, so Menlo, Consolas and Liberation Mono draw different logos from the same SVG. IBM Plex Mono has a real 600, tabular figures and a technical tone close to that system stack, and it can be embedded. A system stack cannot, so outlining is required even after the family is chosen.

Q2.answer: No. Replace DM Sans and DM Mono with IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Mono, self-hosted at 400 and 500.
Q2.why: DM Sans and DM Mono pair with each other but not with the wordmark, and DM Sans is a default AI-dashboard grotesque this system is trying not to look like. DM Mono also lacks the check, cross and triangle glyphs the icon spec sets in the mono face, and it has no 600. One Plex family lets prose, data and the logo be the same product.

top_three: Make every sample state readable without color: a distinct shape per box, a text name, and a running ring that never fades below 3:1.
Specify the missing watch surfaces and the 640px phone breakpoint as tokens and component rules, including focus, keyboard and the drawer.
Remove the contradictions an agent will follow: accent-ink for text, StatusBox colors only, self-hosted fonts, one state-word case, and one outlined wordmark.

issues.problem: Watch is specified as three components, but the drawer, hover card, leaderboard, tabs, theme toggle, empty, disabled and page-loading states are only names in tokens.
issues.why: An agent has to invent layout, copy, keyboard behavior and hit targets for the surfaces watch actually runs on, so two builds will not be the same product.
issues.fix: Add component specs that only use existing tokens plus these values. Drawer: desktop in-flow panel, width 400px, background surface, radius-8, padding space-24, section gap space-28; phone bottom sheet on overlay, top radius-8, shadow-sheet, max-height 85vh, status line 15px. Header is eval-id, a 32×32 × (U+00D7) close, and ‹ › (U+2039/U+203A) sample nav. Esc closes and returns focus; focus is trapped. Assertion rows: radius-6, ✓ (U+2713) in ok or ✗ (U+2717) in red, statement in body-mono. Empty uses help: "This sample has no assertions." Hover card: pointer only, open after 150ms, max-width 280px, padding space-12, radius-8, background overlay, 1px faint border, shadow-hovercard, 8px below the cell (flip if clipped); content is metric, meta, and the marker definition in help. Not on touch; tap opens the drawer. Leaderboard: sticky eval-id column on lbl, one column per arm, row height size-cell, even rows band, best value in accent-ink with a ◆ (U+25C6) prefix, header click sorts with ▼ (U+25BC) in muted. Tabs: height 36px, gap space-28, inactive muted, active fg plus a 2px accent underline. Theme toggle: 36×20px, radius-pill, track raised, 16px surface thumb, accessible name "Dark theme" or "Light theme". Disabled: no opacity fade, text faint, ground raised, aria-disabled, not in tab order. Loading before the first snapshot: percent —, bar at 0 on line, tally "waiting" in muted, no shimmer. Matrix: roving tabindex on cells that are not "not run"; Enter opens the drawer.

issues.problem: Phone sizes and the only breakpoint live in usage prose, while every token value is the desktop number.
issues.why: An agent compiling tokens.css ships 44px counters, 36px cells and 36px side padding on a phone, or invents a second set of sizes.
issues.fix: Add --breakpoint: 640px; --size-cell-phone: 32px; --font-size-counter-phone: 36px; --font-size-counter-finished-phone: 24px; --font-size-heading-phone: 24px; --font-size-status-phone: 15px; --space-page-top: 28px; --space-page-x: 36px; --space-page-x-phone: 16px. Rule text: at max-width 640px use only those tokens; drop the ETA, cell markers and status-box brackets; use size-box-phone. Do not add another breakpoint. Four-arm desktop cells use size-box-phone but keep the brackets.

issues.problem: Pass, fail and timeout are the same filled square, and fail has no marker, so a failed sample is red and nothing else.
issues.why: An agent will ship sample boxes whose pass/fail difference disappears without color, including under the legend, so a color-blind user cannot see which sample failed.
issues.fix: Change the fail row to: filled status-fail square with a 1.5px diagonal slash in the cell ground (raised, or bg if the cell has no fill), so it is not the same shape as pass or timeout. If any sample failed, the cell must also show a bs-mk bs-bad marker reading "fail". Keep timeout as a solid yellow fill plus its warn marker. Add the same slash rule to .bs-b-fail in bundle.css: background linear-gradient(135deg, var(--status-fail) 42%, var(--raised) 42% 58%, var(--status-fail) 58%).

issues.problem: The value style says the best leaderboard figure "takes accent", while the color rules say accent text is always accent-ink and never accent.
issues.why: An agent following the type token will set light-theme best-arm rates in #DF4A19, which the contrast table already measures at 3.72:1 on bg, under the 4.5:1 text floor.
issues.fix: Change the value usage to "the best per row takes accent-ink, never accent". In bundle.css add .bs-best { color: var(--accent-ink); } and use it for the best rate, its ◆ and stars. Keep dark accent-ink #F0764B and light accent-ink #A93F18. Delete any example that colors those strings with accent.

issues.problem: bundle.css imports DM Mono and DM Sans from fonts.googleapis.com, but watch sets default-src 'self', and tokens.json type.fonts is [].
issues.why: An agent who links the component CSS gets no brand fonts under the product CSP and falls back to the system stack, so watch type will not match the spec.
issues.fix: Delete the Google @import. Self-host fonts/DMMono-Regular.woff2, fonts/DMMono-Medium.woff2, fonts/DMSans-Regular.woff2 and fonts/DMSans-Medium.woff2, with @font-face, font-display: swap, and Latin unicode-range. Set type.fonts to those four files at weights 400 and 500 only. If the UI family changes, self-host that family the same way; do not point CSS at a third-party host.

issues.problem: The stylesheet has no :focus-visible rule, and .bs-cell:hover (specificity 0,2,1) overrides .bs-sel so the selected ring shrinks from 2px to 1px.
issues.why: An agent copying bundle.css ships cells whose keyboard focus is the browser default and whose open-drawer state disappears on hover.
issues.fix: Add .bs-cell:focus-visible, .bs-tab:focus-visible, .bs-toggle:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }. Change the hover rule so it sets only background: var(--hover), not box-shadow. Keep .bs-cell.bs-sel, .bs-cell.bs-sel:hover { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--accent); }. Not-run cells are not focusable. Do not set outline: none anywhere else.

issues.problem: Popovers, hover cards and drawers are told to sit on bg, which is the page color and only about 1.1:1 against surface, and the shadow is rgba(0,0,0,0.35).
issues.why: An agent building the default dark theme gets a hover card and phone sheet that blend into #14172E, so the floating layer does not exist.
issues.fix: Add --overlay: #262C4E in dark and #FFFFFF in light, and use it for popovers, hover cards and the phone sheet. Replace the three shadows with dark 0 12px 32px rgba(0,0,0,0.6) and light 0 8px 24px rgba(20,23,46,0.16). Add a 1px solid var(--faint) border on every floating panel so the edge does not depend on the shadow.

issues.problem: The running pulse fades the whole box to opacity 0.45, which blends the accent ring to about 2.9:1 on dark raised, under the 3:1 mark floor.
issues.why: For half of every 1.6s cycle the running sample's ring fails the contrast the table claims, and reduced-motion is the only path that keeps it visible.
issues.fix: Keep the 2px inset ring at opacity 1. Draw the centre dot on .bs-b-run::after (5px circle, status-running) and run bs-pulse on that pseudo-element only. Leave .bs-b-boot and .bs-b-stale unanimated. Keep the reduced-motion rule on the dot.

issues.problem: The one-sentence definition of each sample state exists only as a title attribute on the preview, not in the spec table.
issues.why: An agent treating the README as the spec will omit the legend copy or ship title tooltips, which keyboard and touch users never see.
issues.fix: Add a Definition column to the StatusBox table: pass "Every check in the sample passed."; fail "At least one check failed."; timeout "The agent hit the time cap; its checks were still graded."; error "The sample crashed before it could be graded."; running "The agent is working."; booting "The sandbox is starting or setup.sh is running."; quiet "No output from a running agent for 30s or more."; queued "Waiting for a free worker."; n/a "Every check in this sample runs only on another arm." Render each legend item as a button with a focusable tooltip in the help style. Do not use title.

issues.problem: rate-0 through rate-100 are documented as not yet chosen over status colour, while StatusBox already forbids recolouring pass and specifies the status aliases.
issues.why: An agent that trusts the token file will paint sample boxes on the red-to-green ramp and ship a different watch from one that follows StatusBox.
issues.fix: Replace "not yet chosen over status colour" on every rate-* usage string with "Unused. Do not paint sample boxes from rate-*. Watch uses StatusBox status aliases only." Add that sentence under README Color, Pass-rate ramp. Leave the hex values, but do not reference them from component CSS.

issues.problem: The wordmark is live SVG text in a platform monospace stack, and social-wordmark asks for weight 700 while the type rules allow only 400, 500 and wordmark 600.
issues.why: The logo changes shape between Menlo, Consolas and Liberation Mono, and an agent may synthesize a 700 the face does not have, so README, social card and watch chrome will not match.
issues.fix: Convert the <text> in both wordmark SVGs to outlined paths of IBM Plex Mono at weight 600, baseline y=43, size 30px, starting at x=72. Set social-wordmark fontWeight to 600 and render the social PNG from those paths. Delete the rule that the wordmark must stay live platform text. Keep weight 600 out of the UI; UI stays 400 and 500.

issues.problem: Light band is #E9EBF2, the same hex as light raised, so the light theme has no band step.
issues.why: An agent building the leaderboard gets banded rows in dark and a flat table in light, then invents a third gray to fix it.
issues.fix: Set light --band to #DDE1EB. Keep dark band #181B34, light raised #E9EBF2, light hover #E2E5EF and light lbl #E4E7EF. Recheck text on the new band; fg #1B1F3B and faint #5F667D stay above 4.5:1 because the ground is darker than the old band.

issues.problem: There is no dark-ground mark file, and on light grounds the left squares (#A5ACBE, 2.07:1) and middle square (#F2A48C, 1.83:1) nearly vanish, while size-mark-ui 22px draws the stroke at 1.4px.
issues.why: An agent placing the only mark file on navy loses the brackets, and the light top-bar and social mark read as two orange dots rather than a matrix.
issues.fix: Add benchspec-mark-dark.svg with brackets #E8ECF1, left squares #6E7891, right squares #F0764B and #F2A48C. Theme the light mark: wm-left #6E7891 (about 4.0:1 on brand-paper) and wm-mid #C46A52 (about 3.5:1 on brand-paper); keep dark wm-mid #F2A48C. Raise size-mark-ui and the minimum from 22px to 32px so the 4-unit stroke is 2px. Below 32px, use the word benchspec alone.

issues.problem: Voice rules require uppercase PASS, FAIL, TIMEOUT and ERROR, but the legend, markers and cell labels are all lowercase.
issues.why: An agent will uppercase the legend or lowercase the drawer status line, so the two surfaces will not sound like one product.
issues.fix: Replace the state-words bullet with: uppercase PASS, FAIL, TIMEOUT, ERROR only in the drawer status line and assertion verdicts (FAIL · 6/9 assertions). Legend labels, cell markers and unfinished labels stay lowercase: pass, fail, timeout, error, queued, running, booting, quiet 12s, n/a, not run. The number in quiet 12s is the live duration, never a hardcoded 52s.

Q1.answer: Yes. Adopt IBM Plex Mono (Google Fonts, OFL) at weight 600 and outline it in the wordmark SVGs.
Q1.why: The platform stack is not a brand font: Menlo, Consolas and Liberation Mono draw benchspec differently, and live SVG text will not hold the 250×64 viewBox on every OS. Plex Mono has the 600 the wordmark already specifies; DM Mono does not (400 and 500 only). Its squared technical forms match the bracket mark, and outlined paths keep README, social card and watch chrome identical.

Q2.answer: No. Replace the pair with IBM Plex Sans for prose and IBM Plex Mono for data, and use that same mono for the wordmark.
Q2.why: Watch is a matrix of long eval ids, and DM Mono is wide, so ids truncate early. DM Sans never appears in the wordmark and is a default of generic AI UI, which this system is meant to avoid. Plex Sans and Plex Mono are one free family, with 400/500 for UI and 600 for the mark, and tabular figures. Keep the role split: Plex Mono for counters, cells, ids and tables; Plex Sans for prose, tabs, tooltips and the drawer status line. Self-host both; do not load them from Google at runtime.

top_three: Write the missing watch specs (drawer, hover card, leaderboard, tabs, theme toggle, empty, disabled, loading) and put the 640px phone sizes in tokens so an agent does not invent the product.

Make status and focus hold without color or hover accidents: a slashed fail box plus a fail marker, accent-ink for every accent word, a focus-visible outline that does not collapse the selected ring, and an overlay token so floating panels separate on dark.
Self-host IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Mono, and outline the wordmark in Plex Mono 600, so the CSP, the logo and the UI type are one product on every machine.
